title: Docs: say what a kind's battery is, in one place
body:
### Where?

`kinds/README.md` (the opening paragraph and the `workflows` row of the `pack.yml` table), and the other places that say "battery" without saying what it is: `docs/adopting.md`, `docs/configuration.md` (`workflows` row), `docs/maintaining.md`, the comments of `kinds/*/pack.yml`, `.github/workflows/plugin-checks-wp.yml` and `scripts/sync-repos.py` (`kind_battery()` and its `callers` doc header).

### What is missing, wrong or unclear?

"Battery" (a kind's battery, "ready for the battery") is used across the docs, the packs and the scripts, but no page says what it means. A maintainer reading the autopilot's question on #684 ("where 'ready for the battery' is read from") could not tell what it referred to. The closest is the opening paragraph of `kinds/README.md` ("the list of workflows that make up its battery"), which uses the word as if it were already known, and does not say how the battery differs from the workflows every repository gets, nor that a repository gets the caller that runs it.

### Proposed solution

One definition, in one place, that every other mention links to: in `kinds/README.md`, under "What a pack holds" or as a short "Words" paragraph near the top, say that a kind's battery is the set of reusable workflows that check, test, release and publish a repository of that kind (pack.yml `workflows`, for wordpress-plugin plugin-checks-wp.yml, plugin-tests-wp.yml, plugin-release-wp.yml and plugin-publish-wp.yml); that it is distinct from the workflows every repository gets whatever its kind (repos.yml `every-repository`: conventions, review, pull-request comments); that a repository runs it through its callers, the small files in its own `.github/workflows/` that `scripts/sync-repos.py callers` writes from `workflow-templates/`; and what "ready for the battery" means once #681 settles it (the files the battery needs at the repository's root). The `workflows` rows of `kinds/README.md` and `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/adopting.md`, link to that definition instead of repeating the word bare. If `docs/model.md` keeps a glossary, the term goes there with a link to the same place.

### Problem

A word that only the people who wrote the engine understand makes the autopilot's questions, the drift report and the docs unreadable to everyone else, the maintainer included, and an answer given without understanding the question is a decision taken blind.

### Scope

`kinds/README.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/adopting.md`, `docs/maintaining.md`, and `docs/model.md` only if it has a glossary. Words only: no workflow, script or pack changes.

### Out of scope

What "ready for the battery" checks and where it is read from, which #681 decides. Renaming the term.

### Acceptance criteria

C1: Given `kinds/README.md`, when a reader looks for what a battery is, then one paragraph defines it, names the pack key it comes from (`workflows`), gives the wordpress-plugin example, and says how it differs from the workflows every repository gets and how a repository runs it (its callers).
C2: Given `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/adopting.md` and `docs/maintaining.md`, when they say "battery", then the first mention on each page links to that definition.

### Criticality

Normal

### Who works on it

- [ ] I want to work on this myself

🤖 AI-assisted · Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)

### Spec: approach

Add a short section `## The battery` to `kinds/README.md`, right after the `pack.yml` table in "What a pack holds" (its heading gives the stable anchor `#the-battery`), holding one paragraph that says: a kind's battery is the reusable workflows in `.github/workflows/` that check, test, release and publish a repository of that kind, as listed under the pack's `workflows` key; for wordpress-plugin, `plugin-checks-wp.yml`, `plugin-tests-wp.yml`, `plugin-release-wp.yml` and `plugin-publish-wp.yml`; it differs from the workflows every repository gets whatever its kind (`repos.yml` `every-repository`: `issues.yml`, `pull-request-comments.yml`, and `org-pull-request.yml` that the organisation's ruleset requires) because only a repository of that kind gets it; and a repository runs it through its callers, the files from `workflow-templates/` that `sync-repos.py callers` writes into its `.github/workflows/` and that name the battery's workflows (GitHub cannot pick a reusable workflow from data). The earlier mentions in `kinds/README.md` (intro, the `workflows` row) link to that section.

In `docs/adopting.md` and `docs/maintaining.md`, the first "battery" on each page becomes a link to `../kinds/README.md#the-battery`. `docs/configuration.md` is generated by `scripts/settings.py docs` from `policy/settings-schema.yml` (`test_configuration_doc.py` fails a hand edit), so the link goes into the `says:` of the `workflows` setting there and the page is regenerated with `python3 scripts/settings.py docs > docs/configuration.md`. That is a change of words in a data file under `policy/`, not of a workflow, script or pack; `docs/model.md` has no glossary and no "battery", so it is left alone. Nothing widens any permission, secret, lane or limit.

### Spec: files

- kinds/README.md
- docs/adopting.md
- docs/maintaining.md
- policy/settings-schema.yml (the `says:` of the `workflows` setting only)
- docs/configuration.md (regenerated)
- tests/workflows/test_battery_doc.py (new)

### Spec: tests

- C1 → tests/workflows/test_battery_doc.py
- C2 → tests/workflows/test_battery_doc.py

title: feat: labels.yml lists only the labels that stay
body:
### Problem

Part 5 of #618, the last one. Once parts 1 to 4 moved every counter and step to the board, labels.yml and the repositories still have the retired labels, and nothing stops a new counter or step from becoming a label again.

### Scope

- labels.yml lists only the labels that stay (the allow-list of #618, with its correction: `lane:*` stays), and scripts/sync-repos.py deletes the retired ones from every adopted repository, after checking that none is still on an open issue or pull request.
- A check in scripts/sync-repos.py `--test` fails when a script or workflow sets a label that labels.yml does not list.
- docs/workflows.md and docs/model.md list the labels that stay and say where each retired one's state is.

### Out of scope

- The other parts of #618, each its own sub-issue, done one at a time in the core in the order #618 gives.
- The classification labels (`type:*`, `complexity:*`, `risk:*`, `version:*`, Dependabot's) and the bot's trigger labels, which stay.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given every adopted repository after the sync, when its labels are listed, then they are exactly labels.yml's, and none of the retired labels is left.
- C2: Given a script or workflow that sets a label not listed in labels.yml, when scripts/sync-repos.py `--test` runs, then it fails naming the label and the file.
- C3: Given a retired label still on an open issue or pull request, when the sync runs, then it does not delete that label and says which issue still carries it.

### Criticality

Normal

🤖 AI-assisted · Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)

### Spec: approach

Three pieces, all in `scripts/sync-repos.py` and data it reads:

1. **The retired list as data.** `labels.yml` keeps only the labels that stay (today's list, `lane:*` among them). The labels parts 1 to 4 retired go into a new top-level list in the same file, under `retired:`, each with where its state now is (`{name, now}`): `bug:unconfirmed`, `layer:logic|browser|cli|api|workflow`, `could-not-reproduce`, `repro:no-way` (#801, the board's `repro` state); `enhancement`, `bug` (#803, the issue Type); `needs:maintainer` (#803, `needs-human`); `needs-triage` (#803, the board's `triage` key); `accepted-by:policy`, `merged-by:policy` (#804, the receipts); `autopilot:answered`, `autopilot:catchup`, `autopilot:core-wait`, `autopilot:waiting` and the numbered `autopilot:run-*`, `autopilot:free-*`, `autopilot:round-*`, `autopilot:waiting-*` (#802/#811, the board's flow state; matched by prefix). `scripts/receipts.py` `RETIRED` and sync-repos.py's `RETIRED_FOR_TYPE`/`RETIRED_FOR_LABEL` stay as they are (the migrations still read them); the new list is the one the deletion reads. Because labels.yml becomes a mapping (`labels:` and `retired:`), every reader of labels.yml (`load_yaml(... "labels.yml")` in sync-repos.py, its drift check, and any other script or test that reads it) reads `labels:`.

2. **Deleting the retired labels** (C1, C3). `sync_labels` runs after the existing `retire_labels` and `retire-labels` migrations, then lists the repository's labels once (`gh label list --json name`), and for each one in the retired list asks GitHub for any open issue or pull request still carrying it (`gh api search/issues` or `repos/{full}/issues?state=open&labels=<name>`, which includes pull requests). None: `gh label delete <name> --yes`. Some: the label is kept and the sync prints `label <name> kept: still on #<n>[, #<m>] (open)`, one line per label, so a person or the migrations clear it first. A failed call keeps that label and is counted, as `retire_labels` does; dry run says what it would delete or keep. The drift check (`drift()`) also lists a retired label still present, so the daily drift report shows what is left.

3. **The check** (C2). A function `label_misuse(root)` in sync-repos.py scans `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `workflow-templates/*.yml` and `scripts/*` (outside each script's `--test` block and `scripts/fixtures/`) for the ways a label is *set*: `--add-label X`, `gh issue|pr create ... --label X`, `gh label create X`, `labels[]=X`, and the label-name constants a script sets (`FOUND_BY`, `UNVETTED_LABEL`, …, read as `NAME = "x:y"` next to an add call). Removing, listing or searching a label is not setting it. A literal not in labels.yml's `labels:` is reported as `<file>:<line>: sets label <name>, which labels.yml does not list`; `--test` runs it over the repository and fails on any. A label built from a variable (`--add-label "$l"`, `run:$kind`) is checked through the values it can take where they are written in the same file (the `run:*` kinds, `type:*`, `risk:*`), or is named once in an explicit `dynamic:` list in the check with the file it comes from; unknown dynamic ones fail too, so a new one cannot slip in.

**Decisions for the maintainer.**

A. *What C1's "exactly labels.yml's" deletes.* (a) **Recommended:** only labels.yml's `retired:` list. A label a repository added for itself (GitHub's own `documentation`, `help wanted`, `invalid`, `wontfix`, `good first issue` variants, a project's own labels) stays, as labels.yml's header promises today; C1 is then "every label of labels.yml is there and none of the retired is left". (b) Every label not in labels.yml is deleted, after the same open-item check: C1 literally, but it deletes what repositories' people made and changes the sync's promise. I will build (a) unless told (b).

B. *Labels the code sets today that labels.yml does not list*, which the new check fails on: `repro:retry`, `repro:blocked`, `repro:unblocked`, `repro:broken` (issue-repro.yml, issue-triage.yml), `found-by:dilux-ai` (nightly-review.py), `lane:security-carry` (security-patch.yml), and, in the private security repository only, `security:intake`, `security:unvetted`, `patch:ready|pushed|failed|released|not-released` (triage-act.sh, advisory.py, security-patch.yml); plus the legacy branch in autopilot.yml that still adds `autopilot:run-1` for scripts older than #802. Options: (a) **Recommended:** add the repro, `found-by` and `lane:security-carry` labels to labels.yml (they are live steps the PRD does not retire, and their ad-hoc `gh label create` calls go), give the security repository's labels their own short list in labels.yml (`security-repo:`) that the sync applies only to org.yml's `security` repository and the check accepts, and drop autopilot.yml's pre-#802 `autopilot:run-1` branch (every caller now runs scripts with `FLOW_KEYS`). (b) Move the repro and patch steps to the board as well: a part 6 of #618, outside this PRD's scope; I would stop and ask for its issue. (c) An exception list in the check for them: the check passes, but the labels stay outside labels.yml, which is what the PRD wants to stop.

C. *Closed items.* GitHub deleting a label removes it from closed issues and pull requests too, so their history loses it (labels.yml's comments say "the definitions stay, for closed issues" today). The PRD asks only for open items to be checked, so I will delete regardless of closed items and say so in labels.yml and docs/workflows.md; the receipts and boards keep the state.

### Spec: files

- `labels.yml` (mapping: `labels:` that stay, `retired:` with where each one's state is; header rewritten; option B(a): the repro, `found-by`, `lane:security-carry` labels and a `security-repo:` list)
- `scripts/sync-repos.py` (load `labels:`/`retired:`; `delete_retired_labels()` called from `sync_labels`/`adopt`; drift lists retired labels left; `label_misuse()` and its `--test` cases; usage text)
- `.github/workflows/issue-repro.yml`, `.github/workflows/issue-triage.yml`, `.github/workflows/security-patch.yml`, `scripts/run-issue.sh`, `scripts/triage-act.sh` (option B(a): drop the ad-hoc `gh label create` of labels labels.yml now lists; the security repository's stay created by the sync)
- `.github/workflows/autopilot.yml` (option B(a): drop the pre-#802 `autopilot:run-1` branch)
- other readers of labels.yml found by `grep -rn labels.yml scripts tests .github` (their loading only)
- `docs/workflows.md`, `docs/model.md` (the labels that stay; a table of each retired label and where its state is now; what the sync deletes and when it keeps one)
- `tests/workflows/test_issue_805_labels.py` (new)
- `CHANGELOG` fragment as the repository's changelog-fragments flow asks

### Spec: tests

- C1 → tests/workflows/test_issue_805_labels.py
- C2 → tests/workflows/test_issue_805_labels.py
- C3 → tests/workflows/test_issue_805_labels.py

(C1: `sync_labels` with a fake `gh` whose repository has every labels.yml label plus every retired one and no open item carrying them: every retired one gets `label delete`, none of labels.yml's does, and a repository-added label is left (option A(a)); labels.yml's `retired:` contains each label removed from labels.yml by #801–#811 and none of `labels:`. C2: `label_misuse()` on a temporary tree with a workflow that runs `--add-label not-a-label` returns that label and that file, and on the repository itself returns nothing. C3: the fake lists an open issue #7 carrying `bug:unconfirmed`: no `label delete bug:unconfirmed`, and the output names `#7`. At the base the functions and `retired:` do not exist, so each test fails there.)

### Spec: impact

- Every adopted repository's labels, through `sync-repos.py labels`/`all` and `adopt` (and the daily drift check): the first deleting step the label sync has. Deleting is irreversible for closed items' label history (decision C).
- Every reader of labels.yml: its shape changes from a list to a mapping; sync-repos.py's `sync_labels`, `drift`, its `--test` (the #552 case reads every label), and any test under tests/ that loads it. Missing one breaks the sync for every repository, so all are changed in the same pull request and `make pre-pr` runs every `--test`.
- Sibling code doing the same: `retire_labels` (#803) and `retire_repro_labels` (#801) migrate open issues off retired labels; they run first, so the deletion finds fewer carriers. `receipts.RETIRED` stays the migration's list.
- The workflows that create labels ad hoc (`gh label create ... || true`) in issue-repro.yml, issue-triage.yml, triage-act.sh, run-issue.sh, security-patch.yml: with option B(a) they rely on the sync having run, as `lane:*` already does (sync-repos.py warns when it is missing); a repository not synced yet would fail `--add-label`. To keep that safe, those `gh label create --force` calls may stay where the label is in labels.yml (same colour and description), and the check accepts `label create` of a listed label.
- The new check runs in `scripts/sync-repos.py --test`, so in the scripts job and `make pre-pr` of this repository; a future pull request adding a label without listing it fails there.
- Docs: docs/workflows.md's issue-triage, issue-repro, autopilot rows mention retired labels and `sync-repos.py retire-labels`; they are brought in step.

### Spec: threats

- **Tampering / Elevation (deleting labels):** the sync runs with the App's token over every adopted repository; a wrong `retired:` entry would delete a live label everywhere. Stopped by: the test that `retired:` and `labels:` are disjoint and that every retired name was removed from labels.yml by #801–#811; deletion only of names in `retired:` (option A(a)); the open-item check before each delete; dry run first.
- **Denial of service (the flow):** deleting a label a workflow still adds (a pre-#802 caller) would make `--add-label` fail. Stopped by: the C2 check over this repository's workflows and scripts, and dropping the legacy branch; callers pin the central ref, so an old caller reads old scripts that the release notes cover.
- **Repudiation:** a kept label is printed with the issue that holds it; deletions are printed per repository in the sync's log.
- **Information disclosure:** the sync prints only label names and issue numbers of the repository it syncs; for the private security repository it prints numbers only, as today.
- **Spoofing / inputs:** label names come from labels.yml in this repository (reviewed, merged by a person), never from issue text; names passed to `gh` as separate arguments and URL-quoted in API paths (as `retire_labels` does). The check reads files of this repository only and runs no code from them.
- **Permissions:** no new permission, secret, lane or limit; `gh label delete` uses the same `issues: write` the label sync already has. The pull request says that the sync now deletes labels.

### Spec: architecture

- Data in labels.yml, behaviour in `scripts/sync-repos.py`, as the repository's rule asks (nothing hard-wired: the retired list is data, read by the script). The deletion is a step of the existing `labels` sync, after `sync_labels` and the #801/#803 migrations, following `retire_labels`'s pattern (one call per label, a failed call counted and said, the other repositories go on, dry run supported, idempotent).
- The C2 check lives in sync-repos.py beside the label sync and runs in its `--test`, as the PRD asks; the pytest test under `tests/workflows/` imports it, as `test_issue_803_labels.py` does.
- Must not break: `retire_labels`/`retire_repro_labels` (they still run first), the `lane:*` labels the autonomy lanes and the gate read, the classification labels (`type:*`, `complexity:*`, `risk:*`, `version:*`, Dependabot's) and the bot's trigger labels (`repro:run`, `repro:again`, `spike`, `review:full`, `autopilot:continue`), the drift check's output format, and every other reader of labels.yml.
